title: #4471 review · two causes hidden by one ticket · support kb

#4471 review · two causes hidden by one ticket

owner support desk
proposed
reviewed 2026-10-28 · 0 days ago

The original incident page calls the merged reports one known parser issue. Its rendered components show two causes. Split the work into a shared parser ticket and a booking-v3 date-hint ticket. These are classifications from the export’s executable model; they do not prove that either production fix has shipped.

This review uses the 4 October 2026 export. The desk keeps working. Reconcile new reports and ticket state before applying this split; do not treat this snapshot as today's queue.
Counts from the data

412 reports merged into #4471 · 2 causes

hint	33	hint ×18 · parser ×15	3	2026-04-17 → 2026-09-22	not this ticket — no ticket of its own

5 reports read as a one-day move; filed under parser by tenant.

The export overlaps at page boundaries. Count each report ID once, using the supplied uniqueById, then filter mergedInto === 4471. Classify with causeOf, the tenant’s locale, its booking-form version, and the report channel. Intl.DateTimeFormat supplies locale date order. Browser locale and intake tags are guesses, not the cause. The table and its one-day-move footnote are computed from these inputs on each build.

The reproducible count and complete ID membership are saved in evidence/analysis.json. Published tickets: shared parser, issue #1 and booking-v3 hint, issue #2. The table above describes ticket ownership at export time; the hint now has its own GitHub issue. Local copies are tickets/parser.md and tickets/hint.md.

What each ticket fixes

Shared parser: day-first tenant dates are read month first. For example, R-41200 reports 7 April becoming 4 July. Correct the shared parsing contract and test day-first locales across app, email, and booking-v2 form paths. A booking-v3 tenant’s app or email report still belongs here; form version alone does not determine the cause.

Booking-v3 hint: its date field prints MM/DD/YYYY to day-first tenants while the form reads input in the tenant’s date order. The hint and interpretation disagree. Make the hint match the form’s locale-aware interpretation, and test the form route separately. A shared-parser fix alone does not establish that this mismatch is fixed.

Five desk-noted reports describe one-day moves or related timing anomalies: R-41202, R-41209, R-41236, R-41344, and R-41620. The supplied classifier places them inside the parser total. Keep them there without double counting, but investigate them separately within that ticket. Their wording does not establish a timezone root cause or justify claiming a third confirmed cause. Capture original input, expected and actual dates, timezone, locale, and path before deciding whether to split again.

When reports arrived and when the desk merged them
03-30
04-27

07-20

 received ·  merged into #4471 · per week

Received and merged are different events. Reports arrived from April; the large early-July merge combines an existing backlog. It does not show that the failures began in July, that July had an equivalent arrival spike, or that merging fixed anything. New reports continue through the export date. Inspect both series when deciding priority.

Stop the same merge from happening again

The triage page says to merge on normalized subject alone and to merge when unsure. Decision 0001, accepted in June 2024, records that rule. Its age and the rendered counterexamples require a fresh decision. The accepted decision remains unchanged as history.

Proposed replacement: use subject matches only to find candidates. Compare tenant locale, form version, channel, symptoms, and reproduction evidence. Merge only with evidence of the same cause. Keep unknown tenants and unresolved timing anomalies in review; an unknown cause is not evidence of duplication. Route new reports while the old backlog is being reconciled so they are not silently merged back into the umbrella ticket.

The cases show that identical subjects can hide different causes, different subjects can describe the same cause, and two unknown tenants are not a confirmed match. This exported HTML is a build-time snapshot of the component’s initial state and case results.

Handoff and review

Support owns classification and reconciliation; engineering verifies and fixes each reproduction path. Keep report-to-ticket membership auditable. The two GitHub issues are linked above. Check their status and any new reports before updating this page. Do not mark the bugs resolved merely because the split or this review exists. Once the desk accepts a new dedupe policy, record it as a new numbered decision, link it from triage, and schedule a review with an explicit owner. Rebuild the components after data changes.
